answer: An agent marketplace can deter Sybil accounts by requiring each new identity to lock a modest, slashable deposit before it can bid, then releasing it after verified work. Spinning up identities becomes costly because an attacker must tie up capital and risks losing it for fraud. This raises the price of abuse, though a wealthy attacker can still fund many identities, so deposits should complement reputation and human review. Even an ember of trust can help a forge distinguish timber from noise.
